what: Independent re-check of the steering additions after the review fixes, at 09da2491: two reviewers (code; measurement and documents), each followed by a skeptic who re-checked every finding. Given the code, the first review's record and the documents, not the author's conclusions.

findings.title: The bias-corrected average makes r_heat_peak price the first 1-2 s of F2's window (a short-window maximum over 12 drives), not the hottest drive's 2-20 s RMS
findings.location: hardware/triceratops_build/rl/trike_env.py heat_peak_update() and step() (the `peak_on and self._step_count > self._heat_start_step` block); README 'The steering run's training additions' ('Until about tau it is the running mean since 2 s, F2's own estimator'); PLAN status bullet 'so it prices from the start of F2's window'
findings.evidence: At n=1 the estimate is the square root of one control step's (torque/rating)^2, and the cost takes the maximum of 12 such values. A stride is about 22 steps, so this is a stride-phase sample. I profiled the D22 policies in the script's own setup (rev_hw/heatprof_run.py, extra.py). fore128-s0, seed 100001, 0.15 m/s, deterministic: the F2-style 2-20 s hottest RMS is 0.729, under the 0.8 margin, so F2 sees no excess. The env's estimate is 1.59 at 2.02 s, 1.33 at 2.5 s and 1.08 at 3 s, and 99 % of the episode's r_heat_peak falls in 2-4 s. Over the 4 policies x 3 seeds at 0.15 m/s deterministic, 2-4 s (11 % of the episode) carries 11-100 % of the cost (s1: 0.85/0.93/0.80; s2: 0.57/0.95/1.00). The cost per step is 0.121-0.160 in 2-4 s against 0.000-0.054 in 10-20 s. At 0.25 m/s deterministic, s0 pays 0.118 per step in 2-4 s against 0.063 in 10-20 s. Under noise 0.2 the ratio is about 1.3x. The same correction gives these early steps a large share of the discounted return (A3: 4.4 at 2.02 s, still above 0.5 for 3.4 s). For a cool gait, the term therefore mostly rewards a quiet first second after 2 s, which F2 averages away.
findings.suggested_fix: Price only once the average spans about one tau, or use a partial bias correction. For example, divide by max(1-(1-alpha)^n, 1-(1-alpha)^n0) with n0 of 50-100 steps, or keep averaging from 2 s but price from heat_peak_start_s + 2 s. Add a test that a periodic gait-like input (a 22-step cycle) gives no early cost spike. Re-check with the profile above: the 2-4 s share of the cost should be close to its time share. Re-run steer_heat_weight.py after any change, since the margins include this early cost.

findings.title: The case for dev weight 1 rests on an unmeasured noise level at full scale; at the noise earlier runs had at 1-2 M steps, weight 1 nearly erases the margin and 0.5 only just meets the README's 0.3 rule
findings.location: hardware/triceratops_build/rl/README.md 'The steering run's training additions', bullets 'The noise shrinks as training goes on...' and 'That is the failure the 0.3 margin rule above guards against'; PLAN_STEERING_RUN.md status; DECISION_LOG.md D29
findings.evidence: The README cites D22's final std 0.083-0.091, but that is at 10 M steps. The cost reaches full weight at 3 M (late ramp 1-3 M), and a 3 M dev run ends there. Checkpoints of earlier runs with log_std_init -1.6, read with torch weights_only: run3_dev probe 0.193 (0.5 M), 0.178 (1.0 M), 0.172 (1.5 M); probe_1m_ankleroll 0.193 (1.0 M); pipe1 0.172 (2.0 M). I measured std 0.175 at full scale in the script's exact setup (worst of 4, 3 seeds; my std 0.2 and std 0 rows reproduce the committed numbers exactly). w=1: +0.131 at 0.25 m/s, +0.053 at 0.15 m/s. w=0.5: +0.316 and +0.244. By the 0.3 rule at std 0.175, the compliant range is w <= about 0.5 at 0.25 m/s (0.500 - 0.369 w) and w <= about 0.35 at 0.15 m/s (0.436 - 0.384 w). At the rule's own std 0.2, neither chosen weight meets 0.3 (0.5: +0.147 and +0.021; 1: -0.055 and -0.184). Today's reward (w=0) already misses it at 0.15 m/s (+0.225), which the section does not say. Heavy robots make it worse: at x1.1, std 0.2, w=0.5, 0.15 m/s the margin is +0.003, while the presets train up to x1.23 total mass. During the ramp the margins are comfortable: at late 0.5 (2 M), w=1 gives +0.347/+0.207 at std 0.2 and +0.495/+0.409 at std 0.175. The data do not clearly favour another bracket. 0.5 and 1 are a defensible pair of 'edge of the rule' and 'aggressive', but the docs present 1 as safe.
findings.suggested_fix: Say plainly that the 0.3 rule is relaxed, and on what assumption: weight 1 needs std <= about 0.15 by 3 M, and 0.5 needs about 0.175 or less. In the dev runs, read the action std at 1, 2 and 3 M from train_health.jsonl, re-run steer_heat_weight.py at that std, and only then fix the judged weight. If a rule-consistent pair is wanted instead, 0.25-0.5 is what the data support at std 0.175. Make sure the dev runs are long enough to reach full scale (late ramp to 3 M), otherwise they cannot test this.

findings.title: 'About a third' effective weight is the steady-state value of a plain EMA; with this commit's bias correction the weight is much higher early in the window
findings.location: README 'The steering run's training additions' ('Under gamma 0.99, a step's heat reaches the return with about a third of the weight...'); trike_env.py TrikeEnvConfig comment on w_heat_peak ('0.33 at tau 4 s (0.67 at 1 s...)')
findings.evidence: alpha/(1-0.99(1-alpha)) = 0.334 holds only far from the window start. With the bias-corrected average from 2 s (alpha = 1-exp(-0.02/4)), the discounted weight of one step's heat is 4.43 at 2.02 s, 1.28 at 2.5 s, 0.91 at 3 s, 0.64 at 4 s, 0.47 at 6 s and 0.37 at 10 s. Over the 2-20 s window it averages 0.44 without bootstrapping at the 20 s truncation and 0.47 with it, and it stays above 0.5 for the first 3.4 s.
findings.suggested_fix: Give the profile, or at least 'about 1/3 after the first few seconds; much more just after 2 s', or fix A1, which also removes most of the early concentration.

findings.title: Margins are quoted to three decimals without uncertainty; several are indistinguishable from zero
findings.location: README table and bullets in 'The steering run's training additions'; analysis/results/steer1/heat_weight/heat_weight_margins.md
findings.evidence: The per-seed spread of one policy's margin (std 0.2, w=0.5) gives a standard error of 0.012-0.040 for each 3-seed mean (e.g. s0 at 0.15 m/s: +0.044, +0.043, -0.023). The quoted +0.021 (0.15 m/s, w 0.5) and +0.003 (x1.1) are within one SE of zero, and taking the worst of four noisy means biases the figure down a little.
findings.suggested_fix: Report the per-seed spread or SE beside the worst-of-four margin, and round to two decimals.

findings.title: README says the late and push/friction ramps 'follow TOTAL_STEPS'; they are fixed in absolute steps
findings.location: README 'The presets' bullet: 'the learning rate, the late ramp (1 M to 3 M) and the push and friction ramp (1 M to 4 M) are train.py's, and follow TOTAL_STEPS'
findings.evidence: train.py uses late_scale_at(n, args.late_ramp_from, args.late_ramp_to) and late_scale_at(n, args.terrain_ramp_from, args.terrain_ramp_to) with absolute step counts. Only the learning rate (LinearSchedule over total_steps) follows TOTAL_STEPS. The notebook default TOTAL_STEPS is still 2 M, where the late scale ends at 0.5.
findings.suggested_fix: 'the learning rate follows TOTAL_STEPS; the late ramp (1-3 M) and the push and friction ramp (1-4 M) are fixed in steps, so a run shorter than 3 M never prices heat at full weight'.

findings.title: The bias-corrected heat average is dominated by its first fraction of a second after 2 s. On a real gait it over-prices the 2-3 s window by up to about 4x, and a push early in the push window costs about 3x a late one. The docs describe it as F2's own estimator.
findings.location: hardware/triceratops_build/rl/trike_env.py: heat_peak_update (about line 459), step() lines 968-972, the w_heat_peak config comment (about lines 171-183); rl/README.md, 'The steering run's training additions' (heat bullet)
findings.evidence:
At n = 1 the bias correction makes the estimate one 20 ms step mean. The cost is the max over 12 drives of such short means, so early on it follows the stride phase, not the drive's RMS. Measured on the D22 128 mm policies with the preset heat settings (deterministic, 0.25 m/s, seeds 100000-100002; scratch heat_traj.py, heat_early.py):
- The env's hottest-drive estimate peaks at 1.51-1.79 in 2.0-2.5 s. The true worst-drive RMS over 2-3 s is 0.85-1.05, and over 2-20 s it is 0.81-1.00.
- The per-step cost at w=1 in 2-3 s peaks at 0.17-0.99, against an F2-window steady cost of 0.005-0.20.
- Episode totals exceed the F2-window price x 900 steps: 21.3 against 4.8 (fore128-s0, seed 100001), 63.2/58.9, 162.3/148.6, 145.8/130.8.
- My offline recomputation matches the env to 1e-12. With a 50-step floor on the correction, the totals return to 51.5, 148.7 and 130.7 (scratch variants.py).
- Pushes (push window 3-17 s): a synthetic 0.5 s burst at 2x rating on a drive at 0.7 costs 47.7 per unit w at 3 s, 28.3 at 5 s and 15-17 at 10-15 s, against 1.2 at 3 s in the first version.
- Real pushes with the D22 policies, same seed and push size, only the time changed (scratch push_time.py): a push at 3 s adds -9.5 to +19.0 per unit w (mean +7.3); at 10 s it adds -7.1 to +4.0 (mean -0.3).
- The critic sees neither time nor the average.
- The README and config comment say 'until about tau it is the running mean since 2 s, F2's own estimator' and 'a constant heat gives its own RMS from the first step (tested)'. The test uses only constant inputs. The 'about a third' effective weight holds only after about tau.
- The dev weights 0.5 and 1 were measured with this estimator, so they do not carry over to another one.
findings.suggested_fix:
Choose the estimator before the dev runs, since D29 says they set the weight. Options and their trade-offs on the same logs:
- A floor on the correction, 1 - (1 - alpha)^max(n, ~50): episode totals match the F2-window price and the early peak drops to 0.07-0.25. It does not cheapen a push at 3 s (47.7).
- Average from 2 s but price only from 3-4 s.
- A warm start at margin^2 with no correction: it halves the 3 s burst (23.4) but under-prices by 15-25 %.
- Starting the push window later.
Whichever is chosen: re-run analysis/steer_heat_weight.py (minutes) and re-check the 0.5 and 1 choice. Correct the README and config wording ('F2's own estimator', 'a third'). Add a test with a periodic input, for example a 1 Hz square wave of torque^2, bounding the estimate's overshoot in the first second.

verdicts.reasoning: The mechanism and the numbers hold. With n small, the bias-corrected average is a short-window mean, and the cost takes the maximum of 12 of them, so a gait whose 2-20 s RMS is under the 0.8 margin still pays, almost all of it in the first 1-3 s after 2 s. That goes against the config comment 'RMS / continuous rating below which a drive costs nothing'. The README's 'F2's own estimator' is literally true but misleading: F2 applies that estimator over 18 s, not step by step. There is no test with a periodic input. Two parts are overstated. First, the headline ('prices the first 1-2 s, not the 2-20 s RMS') holds only for gaits near or under the margin. Under training noise the early excess is a small part of the cost: 2 % of the episode's r_heat_peak at std 0.2, 5-7 % at std 0.1. Second, 'a stride is about 22 steps' is wrong. The gait report gives a stride of about 0.68 Hz, about 74 control steps, and a longer stride makes the short-window effect last longer, not shorter. It stays medium: a real defect, limited in effect, with a cheap fix that should go in before the dev runs.

verdicts.reasoning: Every number checks out exactly. It is true that the README rests weight 1 on the final std at 10 M, while the cost reaches full weight at 3 M. It is also true that today's reward (w=0) already misses the 0.3 rule at 0.15 m/s on these policies, which the section does not say. Overstated: the README does not present 1 as safe. It says plainly that weights 1 and 3 fail at the initial noise, and it argues conditionally (+0.31 at std 0.15). The 0.17-0.19 std 'at 1-2 M' comes from short runs (total 1.5-2 M) whose learning rate annealed to the end, and none had r_heat_peak, which itself penalises noise. A log-linear path from 0.2 to the 10 M finals (about 0.085) gives about 0.155 at 3 M. So the std at full scale is unknown and lies between the README's 0.15 and the finding's 0.175. Even at 0.175 both weights keep walking ahead of standing (+0.13/+0.05 at w=1), and the margins during the ramp are comfortable. So the risk is a thinner margin than the rule asks for, not a broken dev run, and bracketing the weight is what the dev runs are for. What remains is a docs gap: an unstated assumption and a silently relaxed rule. Low.

verdicts.reasoning:
The mechanism is real, and every number I checked reproduces exactly. With n = 1 the correction makes the estimate a single 20 ms step mean, so in the first second after 2 s the price follows the stride phase. In the return, a step's heat is weighted 4.4 at 2.02 s, 1.3 at 2.5 s, 0.91 at 3 s, 0.64 at 4 s and 0.47 at 6 s. It settles near 0.33 only from about 8-10 s. So the README's and config comment's unqualified 'about a third' is wrong for the first 3-6 s of the window. Over the whole window its median is 0.36 and its mean 0.44.

A synthetic burst prices about 3x higher at 3 s than at 10-15 s. Several parts of the finding are overstated or wrong:
(1) 'Episode totals exceed the F2-window price x 900' is cherry-picked. Over all 12 deterministic episodes the env totals 1330.6 against 1284.7 (+3.6 %), and 5 of the 12 are below. The 2-3 s window's integrated cost runs from 0.6x to 4.9x the true 2-3 s price, so it is not always an over-price.
(2) 'The test uses only constant inputs' is false. test_heat_peak_update_is_bias_corrected also feeds 30 random inputs and checks the plain running mean, and test_heat_peak_follows_an_independent_recomputation uses real torques under random actions. The overshoot is the specified behaviour of the running mean that the first review's M3 asked for, not an implementation bug.
(3) The real-push evidence comes from 6 of the 12 episodes (s0 and s3 only). With all four policies, trajectory divergence dominates: +4.1 at 3 s against -2.8 at 10 s, a paired difference of +6.9 with SE 4.0.
(4) 'The dev weights do not carry over' is overstated. Under the initial noise (std 0.2) the early overshoot adds only 0.014-0.022 per step at w = 1 (a 50-step floor removes it). That moves the README margins by about 0.01-0.02, far less than the 0.2-0.8 gaps between weights, so 0.5 and 1 would still be chosen.
The suggested floor does not change push costs either: the push deltas with and without it are identical.

Net: the incentive is front-loaded (a cooler start-up and early-push recovery are priced up to 3-13x), and one docs figure ('a third') needs qualifying. Neither wastes the runs or moves the weight choice. The owner should know before freezing the estimator, but this is low, not medium.
